sources.title: National Consumer Helpline: About this portal
sources.locator: Questions 1, 3 and 8; retrieved text lines 21-27, 33-38 and 90-94
sources.summary: Official Department of Consumer Affairs explanation of NCH, complaint channels and the limits of its grievance process.

claims.text: For a consumer grievance, the National Consumer Helpline offers a pre-litigation grievance process.
You can contact NCH on 1915 or register a grievance on its portal. Online filing requires one-time registration and allows supporting documents.
NCH does not guarantee a remedy. If the grievance remains unresolved, a consumer may approach the appropriate Consumer Commission.

sources.title: NALSA: Frequently asked questions
sources.jurisdiction: India; legal services institutions; eligibility and appropriate authority must be checked
sources.summary: Official routes to legal advice and legal-aid applications; the suitable institution depends on location and subject matter.

claims.text: NALSA lists 15100 as its toll-free number for urgent legal assistance.
You may approach an appropriate legal services institution in person, by post, through its online process or by email. District Legal Services Authorities have front offices for applications.

NALSA distinguishes court representation through legal aid from legal advice and assistance; its FAQ says advice and assistance can also be available to people outside legal-aid eligibility categories.

sources.title: NALSA: Legal Aid
sources.jurisdiction: India; free legal aid subject to eligibility and assessment by the relevant institution
sources.locator: Legal Services questions 2 and 4; Eligibility question 1; retrieved text lines 147-159 and 166-178
sources.summary: The official page describes services and eligibility. The prototype does not decide eligibility or quote a universal income threshold.

claims.text: Free legal aid depends on eligibility and assessment of the case by the relevant Legal Services Authority. Income-based criteria can depend on the state and court.
Legal-aid services may include an advocate's representation, preparation of documents and certain proceeding-related expenses.
